# RCP — REST Connector Protocol | Expose REST API as AI Tools Without MCP Server

> A lightweight, open protocol for exposing REST APIs as AI-callable tools — without running a protocol server. RCP is the stateless HTTP alternative to Model Context Protocol (MCP) for OpenAI, LangChain & Gemini tool calling. Your REST API is already the tool — just add a manifest.

RCP (REST Connector Protocol) is an open standard and TypeScript SDK for turning existing REST APIs into AI-callable tools. A server publishes a plain JSON manifest at `GET /manifest`. A client fetches it, builds callable tools from it, and calls the endpoints it describes directly — no JSON-RPC, no persistent connection, no protocol server. Published as `rcp-sdk` on npm.

## Docs

- [Introduction: What is RCP?](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs): What is REST Connector Protocol, design principles, two roles (Client/Server), no persistent connection
- [Getting Started: Expose REST API to AI in 5 Minutes](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/getting-started): Install rcp-sdk, define tool with defineTool(), serve manifest, discover & call with createRcpClient()
- [Full Spec: RCP v0.1 Protocol Specification](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/spec): Complete spec — manifest format, resolvers, auth (none/header/oauth2), security & trust
- [RCP vs MCP: Lightweight Alternative to Model Context Protocol](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/vs-mcp): Comparison table, when to use RCP vs MCP, stateless vs stateful, no protocol server
- [Examples: Express + OpenAI & Minimal Demo](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/examples): Working Express REST API + OpenAI tool-calling loop, minimal plain Node http demo
- [Roadmap: v0.1 Done vs Planned](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/roadmap): Implemented vs planned — OAuth2, Python SDK, CLI

## Concepts

- [The Manifest: JSON Directory of AI Tools](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/concepts/manifest): GET /manifest returns { rcpVersion, auth, tools[] } — url, params, queryParams, responseMappings
- [Resolvers: Hide Tenant ID & User ID from LLM](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/concepts/resolvers): Resolver-bound params stripped from exposedParams at discovery, filled from trusted context at call time
- [Auth: none, header & OAuth2](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/concepts/auth): Three auth modes plus client-injected headers for tracing/tenant isolation

## SDK Reference

- [Client — rcp-sdk/client: createRcpClient, discover() & call()](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/sdk/client): createRcpClient() with resolvers/auth, discover(manifestUrl), call(tool, args), describeManifest()
- [Server — rcp-sdk/server: defineTool()](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/sdk/server): defineTool() with Zod schema, t.arg(), queryParams, responseMappings — turn REST endpoint into AI tool
- [OpenAI Adapter — Connect REST API to ChatGPT](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/sdk/openai): rcpToolsToOpenAiTools() to ChatCompletionTool[] for openai.chat.completions.create()
- [LangChain Adapter — DynamicStructuredTool](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/sdk/langchain): rcpToolsToLangChainTools() to LangChain DynamicStructuredTool, LangGraph, MultiServerRcpClient
- [Gemini Adapter — Google GenAI Function Calling](https://rcp.hasanraiyan.me/docs/sdk/gemini): rcpToolsToGeminiInteractionsTools() & classicTools for Gemini 2.5 Interactions + generateContent

## Quick Start

```bash
npm install rcp-sdk
```

```typescript
// Server: expose REST endpoint as AI tool
import { defineTool } from 'rcp-sdk/server';
import { z } from 'zod';
export const getWeather = defineTool({
  name: 'get_weather',
  description: 'Get current weather for a city',
  method: 'GET',
  args: z.object({ city: z.string().describe('City name') }),
  url: 'https://api.example.com/weather',
  queryParams: { city: (t) => t.arg('city') },
});

// Client: discover + call
import { createRcpClient } from 'rcp-sdk/client';
const client = createRcpClient();
const { tools } = await client.discover('https://api.example.com/manifest');
const result = await client.call(tools[0], { city: 'Paris' });
```
